extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, publishers, news/blog authors, complainants and the general public in Aotearoa New Zealand
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements from the New Zealand Media Council for evaluating journalistic content and for lodging/resolving complaints about newspapers, magazines, websites and other digital media in Aotearoa New Zealand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / Objective: independent forum for resolving complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council’s main objective is to provide the public with an independent forum for resolving complaints involving newspapers, magazines and websites of such publications and other digital media; and to promote media freedom and maintain the press in accordance with the highest professional standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers print and digital publications (newspapers, magazines, websites and other digital media); the Council is an industry self-regulatory body established to resolve complaints and promote professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: support trust in media and freedom of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Our purpose: To support trust in media and freedom of expression by upholding high standards of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council frames its work around both upholding standards and protecting free expression; these aims guide complaint handling and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent press responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent press plays a vital role in a democracy. The proper fulfilment of that role requires a fundamental responsibility to maintain high standards of accuracy, fairness and balance and public faith in those standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and publishers are expected to maintain accuracy, fairness and balance to sustain public trust in the press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of freedom of expression and public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: In dealing with complaints, the Council will give primary consideration to freedom of expression and the public interest; freedom of expression and freedom of the media are inextricably bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When weighing complaints, protection of expression and the public interest can outweigh other concerns; this is a core consideration in rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public interest is defined as involving a matter capable of affecting the people at large so that they might be legitimately interested in, or concerned about, what is going on, or what may happen to them or to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition when assessing whether publication, or withholding information, serves the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous analysis — distinction between fact and opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctions between fact, on the one hand, and conjecture, opinion or comment, on the other hand, must be maintained. This does not prevent rigorous analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications may adopt a forthright stance or advocate on issues, but should clearly separate factual reporting from commentary or opinion. The Council recognises that genre/purpose (blogs, satire, cartoons, gossip) calls for special consideration in complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement of Treaty and Bill of Rights principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Media Council endorses the Principles and spirit of the Treaty of Waitangi and Bill of Rights Act, without sacrificing the imperative of publishing news and reports that are in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council decisions should be aware of and consistent with these constitutional/ethical commitments while still considering public interest publication needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical journalism and editorial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors have the ultimate responsibility for what appears in their publications, and for adherence to the standards of ethical journalism which the Council upholds. News bloggers and digital media are similarly required to participate responsibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council seeks the co‑operation of editors and publishers in resolving complaints; responsibility extends to bloggers and digital media actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Columns, Blogs, Opinion and Letters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognises that opinion formats have different expectations — e.g., more tolerance for advocacy — but factual accuracy and clear labelling remain important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint filing requirements and consent obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants are required to read the Complaints Procedure in full; comply with the Media Council’s service charter; agree with the complaint’s procedure; consent to the privacy statement and the publishing of the ruling on the website; and agree to waive rights to take other proceedings in any way related to the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before lodging a complaint, complainants must ensure they accept procedural terms (service charter, consent to publish rulings, privacy statement) and the waiver of other proceedings; read the full Complaints Procedure for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Principles by complainants / flexibility of ethical grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Principles may be used by complainants when they wish to point the Council to the core of their complaint. However, a complainant may nominate other ethical grounds for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants can invoke the listed Principles or propose alternative ethical bases for a complaint; the Council will consider nominated grounds.
